source_name: KELER – Financial Reports (English mirror)
why_relevant: English-language mirror of KELER's annual/IFRS consolidated financial statements (2020-2024 observed). Removes translation risk for cross-country comparison of post-trade infrastructure economics.

source_name: KELER KSZF Zrt. – Pénzügyi jelentések (CCP annual reports)
why_relevant: Annual reports of the Hungarian central counterparty (EMIR-authorised CCP) covering capital markets, energy and gas market clearing. Deep archive observed (2012, 2013, 2018, 2022 PDFs directly linkable), enabling a long time series on cleared volumes and default-fund sizing.

source_name: KELER KSZF – Financial Reports (English)
why_relevant: English CCP key-documents section; typically also carries EMIR public quantitative disclosures alongside the financial reports.

source_name: KELER KSZF – Közérdekű adatok (public-interest data disclosure)
why_relevant: Statutory public-interest disclosure page for a state/MNB-linked entity: typically lists contracts above the disclosure threshold, procurement, organisational data and executive remuneration — a rare window on vendor relationships of a post-trade operator.

source_name: KELER / KELER KSZF – Jogi környezet (legal environment pages)
why_relevant: Maps the CSDR/EMIR and Hungarian legal instruments that force disclosures by these operators — useful for predicting what documents must exist and when they must be published.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Számviteli beszámolók (accounting reports)
why_relevant: Audited annual accounts of the state-owned postal operator, which is also a major payment service provider (postal money orders, cash-in/cash-out, government-securities distribution). Segment notes are the only public quantification of postal payment volumes and revenue.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Aktualitások / press releases (results, dividend, financial services)
why_relevant: Posta's press releases carry headline results ahead of the full report (e.g. 2024 after-tax profit ~HUF 5.2bn, first dividend since 2009, HUF 1,355bn government-securities stock distributed). Earliest public earnings signal for the postal payments arm.

source_name: Magyar Posta – Pénzforgalmi Üzletszabályzat és ÁSZF (payment services rulebook)
why_relevant: Defines the postal payment product set, fees and the operational role of the Posta Elszámoló Központ (Posta Clearing Centre). Versioned PDFs allow tracking of product retirement/launch and pricing over time.

source_name: Magyar Posta – Posta Elszámoló Központ, pénzforgalmi adatszolgáltatás
why_relevant: The only located public page naming and describing the Posta Elszámoló Központ (PEK) and its data-service function, including its contact/submission channels. Establishes PEK as a distinct operational unit rather than a separate legal entity.

source_name: Magyar Posta – Fenntarthatósági jelentések (sustainability/ESG reports)
why_relevant: CSRD-era sustainability reports of a state-owned operator often disclose network size, branch counts, digitalisation KPIs and IT investment narratives absent from the statutory accounts.

source_name: MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés (Payment Systems Report)
why_relevant: Annual central-bank report (published since 2014, HU and EN) that is the authoritative consolidated statement on VIBER, BKR/GIROInstant, KELER and KELER KSZF operation, availability, incident counts and volumes. Effectively the public 'annual report' for VIBER, which as an MNB-operated system has no standalone corporate report.

source_name: MNB Felvigyázás (payment system oversight) portal
why_relevant: Oversight landing page that indexes the designated systemically important systems, oversight assessments and the quarterly interactive tables on supervised systems' traffic. Best pointer to all MNB-side disclosures about GIRO, KELER and VIBER.

source_name: MNB statisztika – Bankközi fizetési és elszámolási rendszerek forgalma (VIBER, BKR, Posta)
why_relevant: Structured time series of interbank system turnover covering VIBER, BKR, InForex and Posta (archive back to 2002-2010, with current series in the payments-data section). Machine-readable volume/value data that no operator annual report matches for granularity.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár / OPTEN company profiles (GIRO Zrt.)
why_relevant: Commercial company-registry aggregators giving ownership, registration number (e.g. GIRO cg. 01-10-041159 / id e10478384), officers and filed financial summaries — useful for confirming legal identity and ownership chains of the infrastructure operators before pulling their reports.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság / Közbeszerzési Értesítő + EKR (public procurement gazette)
why_relevant: State- and MNB-owned infrastructure operators are contracting authorities; their IT tenders, awards and contract summaries appear only here and in EKR. This is the earliest and most concrete signal of modernisation spend that annual reports mention only in narrative form.

source_name: eGov Hírlevél – GIRO Zrt. tag
why_relevant: Public-sector digitalisation newsletter tracking GIRO's role in e-government payment rails; a low-noise secondary feed for state-side integration projects.

source_name: GIRO karrierportál (giro.karrierportal.hu)
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: GIRO's job postings expose the technology stack, in-flight programmes and team build-outs (e.g. fraud analytics, ISO 20022, cloud) long before any report describes them.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide Investor Relations - SEC filings (10-K/10-Q/8-K)
why_relevant: Euronet was founded as a Hungarian company in 1994 and its Budapest processing centre is still named among EFT Processing segment processing centres in recent 10-Ks; Hungary appears explicitly in risk factors, property and segment discussion. This is the single most auditable disclosure channel for the independent ATM/processing layer in Hungary.

source_name: SEC EDGAR - Euronet Worldwide Inc. company filings archive (CIK 0001029199)
why_relevant: Authoritative archive and full-text-searchable back catalogue of every Euronet filing back to the 1998 10-K, which documents the Hungarian origin, the 1995 Budapest processing centre and the 2003 sale of 272 Hungarian ATMs - i.e. a longitudinal record of Hungarian ATM/processing economics unavailable elsewhere.

source_name: Euronet Magyarország ATM site - Sajtóközlemény (press releases)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language operational announcements of the local Euronet entity (Euronet Banktechnikai Szolgáltató Kft.): network size (~500-600 ATMs), euro-dispensing ATM counts, Community ATM programme for municipalities, deposit-capable ATMs. Gives country-level operating detail the US 10-K aggregates away.

source_name: Mastercard Europe Newsroom (press releases, incl. Hungary items)
why_relevant: Scheme-level European newsroom carrying Hungary-specific releases (e.g. Digital Payments Index country scores, contactless penetration claims such as >95% of Hungarian terminals). Primary vendor-sourced statistics on Hungarian card usage.

source_name: Mastercard Magyarország corporate site (mastercard.hu)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language scheme presence; product, interchange/fee and FAQ pages plus local campaign material. Useful for local terminology harvesting and for scheme fee/product changes announced only in Hungarian.

source_name: Visa Magyarország - Visa szerkesztőség / press releases
why_relevant: Visa's Hungarian press-release hub - announcements of Hungary-specific programmes (e.g. Visa Digital Payments Program offering merchants free online card acceptance) and consumer survey statistics. The scheme-side counterpart to Mastercard's country PR.

source_name: Visa Inc. Investor Relations / annual report (CEE context for Hungary)
why_relevant: Visa does not break out Hungary, but 10-K/annual report and CEMEA commentary frame regional volume growth, interchange regulation exposure and litigation that constrain the Hungarian acquiring economics. Background/normalising layer rather than a country data source.

source_name: Global Payments Magyarország (globalpayments.com/hu-hu)
why_relevant: Global Payments entered Hungary in September 2014 by taking over Erste's POS network and remains a principal acquirer/processor; the Hungarian site carries product, terminal and pricing pages plus local announcements (e.g. softPOS with Erste).

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG press releases (JV / merchant acquiring, CEE)
why_relevant: Group-level, deal-grade disclosure of the Global Payments/CaixaBank/Erste merchant-acquiring JV (2015 announcement, 2016 closing, later country extensions), including stake percentages and consideration. Establishes the corporate structure behind Hungarian acquiring even where Hungary is added later.

source_name: Worldline Magyarország - press releases / media relations (hu-hu)
why_relevant: Worldline (which absorbed SIX Payment Services, present in Hungary since 2009 with 11,000+ merchants) is a major non-bank acquirer in Hungary; the Hungarian media-relations tree carries localised versions of group announcements plus statements of Hungarian market ambition.

source_name: SIX Payment Services Hungary legacy site (six-payment-services.com/hu)
why_relevant: Legacy brand estate still serving Hungarian merchants and documenting the pre-Worldline acquiring footprint (present in Hungary since 2009, 11,000+ merchants). Useful for historical continuity and for merchant-contract terms that still reference the old entity.
